title: Tor amplitude for a finite ring is detected by its Jacobson quotient
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $X$ a scheme, and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $J=\operatorname{Jac}(A)$, the intersection of its maximal ideals, and let $\kappa_X$ be the constant sheaf [def-kun-constant-sheaf] with value $A/J$. For every pair of integers $a,b$, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ against every module sheaf [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if $\mathcal H^q(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa_X)=0$ for every $q<a$ or $q>b$, with the ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. No boundedness or constructibility assumption on $K$, and no inequality between $a$ and $b$, is required.

source.place: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_iff_tensorSingleConcentratedIn; general finite-ring strengthening of the residue test.

proof.text: The forward implication is the defining all-sheaf test, applied to the constant Jacobson quotient. For the converse, a finite ring is Artinian. Its Jacobson radical J is nilpotent, finitely generated by its finite set of elements, and A/J is semisimple. The attached source theorem uses the Mathlib instances IsSemiprimaryRing.isNilpotent and IsSemisimpleRing for this finite-ring specialization.

source.place: Finite Jacobson radical and the forward implication

proof.text: Choose a complex P of flat sheaves which is K-flat and represents K. First let F be killed by J. The ordinary tensor kappa_X tensor F is F: express A/J as the cokernel of the finite row of its generators, apply the right-exact constant-sheaf functor and tensor with F; the row becomes zero. Every monomorphism of sheaves whose target is killed by J splits sectionwise as an A-module map, because its target is a module over the semisimple ring A/J. Hence tensor with F preserves these monomorphisms, after exact sheafification. Together with right exactness this preserves exactness of complexes of J-annihilated sheaves. Apply this to P tensor kappa_X, which is exact outside [a,b]. Its further tensor with F is P tensor F by associativity and the preceding quotient identity. This proves the claimed bound for F killed by J.

source.place: Proof of the ideal residue criterion and its sheaf inputs; no principal-ideal hypothesis

proof.text: For arbitrary F use the finite filtration by J^s F. More explicitly, the image JF of the map from the finite sum of copies of F given by generators of J is killed by J^m whenever F is killed by J^(m+1), while F/JF is killed by J. The resulting short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle after placing in degree zero and tensoring with K. Induction on the nilpotence exponent propagates the [a,b] homology bound from the quotient to F. At exponent zero F is zero; this also verifies the zero ring and empty-interval cases. Thus the bound holds for every F.

source.place: Induction on the nilpotent ideal filtration
